result.title: Jacobian-Causal Memory Control for Persistent Memory in Language Model Systems
result.comment: Architecture and formal analysis preprint. Four conditional theorems; no benchmark measurements. Companion research essay: https://achiral.ai/research/jacobian-causal-memory-control
result.summary: Persistent-memory systems choose not only which records are retrieved but which prior information can alter current inference. We propose Jacobian-causal memory control (JCMC), which represents each authorized memory intervention by a predicted influence signature in a shared behavioral measurement space, selects interventions against a target effect and side-effect budget, and compares predicted with observed effects before retaining or rolling back the intervention. Under explicit smoothness and bounded-estimation assumptions, we prove a quadratic local-approximation bound, characterize the target effects reachable by a set of signatures, bound selection regret under signature error, and bound non-additive interactions between simultaneous memories. The paper reports no benchmark measurements; it defines a paired counterfactual estimator and an evaluation protocol comparing JCMC with relevance, graph, and policy-filtered retrieval baselines. The central claim is narrowed or falsified if those simpler baselines match effect targeting, side-effect control, and rollback utility under equal model, memory, policy, and cost budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Jacobian-causal memory control（JCMC）：以共享行为测量空间中的预测影响签名刻画每次被授权的记忆干预，按目标效应与副作用预算选择干预，并在保留或回滚前比对预测与观测效应；同时给出局部二次近似、可达效应集合、选择遗憾及非可加交互的理论界，但报告无基准实测。
AI.relevance_reason: 「影响签名—效应预算—预测与观测校验—回滚」这一干预式框架，可能为 LVR 中 latent 更新的因果贡献分配与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益成本权衡提供可核查线索；但该工作为纯文本记忆控制的纯理论稿，能否迁移到视觉推理状态尚待验证。
